ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Two parallel metal rails $AM$ and $CP$ are placed horizontally with a spacing of $d$. The right ends of the metal rails are smoothly connected to vertically placed insulating circular rails $MN$ and $PQ$ with a radius of $R$. In the region $EMPF$, there exists a uniform magnetic field directed vertically upward with a magnetic induction strength of $B$. The left boundary $EF$ of the magnetic field is at a distance of $R$ from $AC$. A metal rod $a$ is placed at the position $AC$, and a metal rod $b$ is placed near the left side of $MP$. The masses of the metal rods $a$ and $b$ are $2m$ and $m$, respectively. A horizontal force $F = 32mg$ is applied to the metal rod $a$. When the metal rod reaches the boundary of the magnetic field, the external force is removed. After some time, the metal rod $b$ passes through the highest point of the circular rail, at which point the total normal force exerted by the two circular rails on $b$ is $F_N = 3mg$. Friction between the metal rods and the rails is negligible.

1. What is the velocity of metal rod $a$ when it enters the magnetic field?
2. What is the velocity of metal rod $a$ when metal rod $b$ exits the magnetic field?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are two horizontal parallel metal rails, the upper rail is labeled from A to M, and the lower rail is labeled from C to P. On the left side there is a metal rod a, and the arrow indicates that it moves to the right; the distance between the rails is d. The magnetic field region is enclosed by the left boundary EF and the right boundary MP, and in the figure multiple upward arrows are used to mark the magnetic induction intensity B. EF is located to the right of AC, and the problem gives that the distance from AC to EF is R. The right ends M and P are smoothly connected to a vertically placed insulating circular track, and the radius of the circular track is R; metal rod b is located in the magnetic field region near the left side of MP, and afterward it can leave the magnetic field from MP and enter the circular track. Reasoning: Before metal rod a enters the magnetic field between AC and EF, only the horizontal external force F=32mg does work, the displacement is R, and the mass of rod a is 2m. By the kinetic energy theorem: 32mg·R=(1/2)(2m)v_0^2, so v_0^2=32gR, obtaining that the speed when a enters the magnetic field is v_0=sqrt(32gR). Find the speed when b leaves the magnetic field, that is, reaches MP. When b passes through the highest point of the circular track, the total support force of the two circular tracks on b is F_N=3mg. At the highest point, both gravity and the support force point toward the center of the circle, therefore mg+3mg=m v_top^2/R, giving v_top^2=4gR. The highest point is 2R higher than MP. Neglecting friction, by conservation of mechanical energy: (1/2)m v_b^2=(1/2)m v_top^2+mg(2R), hence v_b^2=4gR+4gR=8gR, namely v_b=sqrt(8gR). During the interaction process from a entering the magnetic field to b reaching MP and leaving the magnetic field, there is no external impulse in the horizontal direction, and the horizontal momentum of the system is conserved. In the initial state only a moves with v_0, and in the final state the speed of a is v_a and the speed of b is v_b, so 2m v_0=2m v_a+m v_b. Substituting v_0=sqrt(32gR) and v_b=sqrt(8gR), obtain v_a=(2sqrt(32gR)-sqrt(8gR))/2=sqrt(18gR).
